llc.formation_notes: Optional expedite (on top of the statutory fee): $100 same-day, $300 3-hour, $1,000 1-hour. No publication requirement found on the DOS fee page.

annual_report.name: Annual Report
annual_report.due: January 1 to September 30 each year for LLCs (domestic and foreign); requirement began in 2025
annual_report.late_penalty: Beginning with reports due in 2027, failure to file leads to administrative dissolution/termination/cancellation six months after the deadline; domestic reinstatement $35 online ($40 paper) plus $15 per missing annual report

state_tax_on_llc.name: Capital Stock/Foreign Franchise Tax
state_tax_on_llc.notes: Eliminated for tax years beginning Jan. 1, 2016 and after. No PA franchise or minimum tax on LLCs; a disregarded or partnership LLC files PA-20S/PA-65 (partnership) or flows to PA-40.

sources.title: PA Department of State - Fees and Payments
sources.quote: Certificate of Organization $125; All other annual reports (for profit entities) $7

sources.title: PA Department of State - Annual Reports
sources.quote: The deadline for limited liability companies (domestic and foreign) is September 30.

sources.title: PA Revenue - Corporation Tax Rates
sources.quote: Eliminated for tax years beginning Jan. 1, 2016 and after.

entity_level_taxes.name: Corporate Net Income Tax on net recognized built-in gains only
entity_level_taxes.notes: A federal S corp is automatically a PA S corporation (can elect out on REV-976, then taxed as C corp). CNIT 7.49% for tax years in 2026, scheduled down each year to 4.99% from 2031. No capital stock tax (eliminated 2016).

sources.title: PA Personal Income Tax Guide - Pass Through Entities
sources.quote: any corporation with a valid federal S corporation election is automatically a PA S Corporation.

personal_exemption.notes: No standard deduction or personal exemption. Low-income Tax Forgiveness credit (Schedule SP) exists; thresholds not collected.

income_tax_2026.starting_point: own definition (eight classes of income; a loss in one class cannot offset another class, no carryforward/back)

sources.title: PA Revenue - Personal Income Tax
sources.quote: The Pennsylvania personal income tax does not provide for a standard deduction or personal exemption.

sources.title: PA Revenue - Personal Income Tax Rates

estimated_tax.required_if: expect at least $430 of PA tax ($14,000 of income not subject to employer withholding) for 2026, and withholding/credits below the smaller of 90% of 2026 tax or 100% of 2025 net PA taxable income x 3.07%

unemployment_2026.notes: Newly liable non-construction employer total rate .038220 (3.5% basic rate + 9.2% surcharge; additional contributions do not apply). Employee UC withholding 0.07% on all gross wages, no cap. Construction new employers higher (not collected).

local_taxes.name: Net Profits Tax (NPT)
local_taxes.applies: Net profits of unincorporated businesses/self-employed: residents on all business income even if conducted outside Philadelphia; non-residents on business conducted in Philadelphia (non-resident rate 3.425%). Tax year 2026, filed in 2027.
local_taxes.threshold_or_exemption: No threshold; a return must be filed even at a loss. Credit against NPT of 60% of the BIRT net income portion paid. Tax year 2025 rates were 3.74% / 3.43%.
local_taxes.quote: For tax year 2026, the Net Profits Tax (NPT) rate will be: Philadelphia residents: 3.735% (down from 3.74%)

local_taxes.name: Business Income and Receipts Tax (BIRT)
local_taxes.applies: Every business (including sole proprietors and LLCs) doing business in Philadelphia: 5.65% of taxable net income PLUS 1.395 mills ($1.395 per $1,000) of gross receipts, tax year 2026 (filed by April 15, 2027).
local_taxes.threshold_or_exemption: The $100,000 gross receipts exemption no longer applies from tax year 2025 (legal challenge). Tax year 2025 rates: 1.410 mills and 5.71%. Scheduled cuts each year; gross receipts portion 0 and net income 2.80% from 2038.
local_taxes.quote: 2026 1.395 mills on gross receipts and 5.65% on taxable net income

local_taxes.name: Wage Tax / Earnings Tax
local_taxes.applies: Wages paid to residents (3.735%) and to non-residents working in Philadelphia (3.425%) from July 1, 2026 to June 30, 2027 - relevant to an S corp owner's salary.
local_taxes.quote: 3.735% for residents of Philadelphia, or 3.425% for non-residents.

local_taxes.place: Pennsylvania (all municipalities and school districts outside Philadelphia)
local_taxes.name: Local Earned Income Tax (EIT) on wages and net profits
local_taxes.applies: Residents on earned income and net profits of a business as sole proprietor or partner; non-residents taxed at work location. Rate varies by PSD code (DCED lookup); 1% is the usual combined cap, shared 50/50 between municipality and school district.
local_taxes.threshold_or_exemption: Cap can be exceeded by home rule municipalities, financially distressed municipalities, Act 24/Act 50 referendum school districts, etc. Annual final return due April 15; residents with net profits over $12,000 must file a declaration and pay quarterly estimates (April 15, July 15, Oct 15, Jan 15).
local_taxes.quote: all other municipalities and school districts adopting income taxes under the Local Tax Enabling Act are limited to a combined rate of one percent.

local_taxes.name: Local Services Tax (LST)
local_taxes.applies: Flat per-person tax on people working in a subdivision, self-employed included (quarterly prorated where rate exceeds $10). Maximum $52 per year.
local_taxes.threshold_or_exemption: Where the rate exceeds $10, mandatory exemption if total earned income and net profits in the subdivision are below $12,000.
local_taxes.quote: The total LST paid by any taxpayer in a calendar year remains limited to $52.

local_taxes.name: Earned Income Tax (city 1% + School District of Pittsburgh 2%)
local_taxes.applies: Residents of Pittsburgh on earned income and net profits; collected by Jordan Tax Service. Non-PA residents working in the city pay 1%.
local_taxes.threshold_or_exemption: Home rule city above the 1% Act 511 cap.
local_taxes.quote: Residents pay 1% city tax and 2% school tax for a total of 3%.

local_taxes.name: Payroll Expense Tax
local_taxes.applies: Employers' gross payroll for work in the city, plus net distributions/draws to self-employed individuals and partners for services performed in Pittsburgh (form ET-1, quarterly).
local_taxes.threshold_or_exemption: Amounts of $2.00 or less not due.
local_taxes.quote: Line 2b (Self-Employed) & Line 3b (Partners) - Multiply line 2a and/or 3a by 0.0055

local_taxes.name: Local Services Tax
local_taxes.applies: $52 per year per person working in the city, employers and self-employed individuals (form LS-1, quarterly).
local_taxes.threshold_or_exemption: Upfront exemption when total earned income from all sources within Pittsburgh is less than $12,000.
local_taxes.quote: Pennsylvania Act 7 of 2007 requires that the $52 be deducted evenly from paychecks throughout the year.

notable: Flat 3.07% PIT with no standard deduction or personal exemption, and a business loss cannot offset wages or other classes of income (https://www.pa.gov/agencies/revenue/resources/tax-types-and-information/personal-income-tax)

New $7 annual report since 2025 (LLCs due Sept 30); missing reports due from 2027 lead to administrative dissolution (https://www.pa.gov/agencies/dos/programs/business/types-of-filings-and-registrations/annual-reports)

Estimated-tax income threshold rising fast: $14,000 in 2026, $17,000 in 2027, $20,000 in 2028 (https://www.pa.gov/content/dam/copapwp-pagov/en/revenue/documents/formsandpublications/formsforindividuals/pit/documents/2026/2026_rev-413i.pdf)

Philadelphia lost the $100,000 BIRT exemption from tax year 2025, so even small freelancers owe BIRT on all receipts; 60% of the BIRT net-income portion is credited against NPT (https://www.phila.gov/media/20251028121348/Philadelphia-business-tax-changes-starting-in-FY26.pdf)

Self-employed people pay local EIT on net profits (usually ~1%, 3% in Pittsburgh, NPT 3.735% in Philadelphia) on top of the 3.07% state tax (https://dced.pa.gov/download/act-32-of-2008-procedure-manual/?wpdmdl=56767)
Pittsburgh also taxes self-employed draws/distributions at 0.55% payroll expense tax (https://www.pittsburghpa.gov/City-Government/Finance-Budget/Taxes)
uncertain: PTET: no Pennsylvania pass-through entity elective tax found on pa.gov; 2023 bills (SB 659) not shown enacted. Set to null, but absence not confirmed by an official statement.

Phila.gov BIRT service page still shows rates only through tax year 2025; 2026 BIRT (1.395 mills / 5.65%) and NPT (3.735% / 3.425%) taken from the phila.gov Tax Rate History page and the 2026-06-11 phila.gov notice, which agree.
A phila.gov FY26 flyer prints the 2025 gross receipts rate as 1.140 mills; the official rate table says 1.410 mills (flyer typo).

Local EIT: rate depends on the exact PSD code; the DCED rate table (PDF download) did not expose rates in extracted text and munstats.pa.gov lookup was unreachable, so only the 1% general cap and Pittsburgh 3% are recorded.
Pittsburgh EIT 3% is from the city Taxes page (not the regulations); non-resident handling for PA residents (higher of home rate or work-location rate under Act 32) not detailed.
Tax Forgiveness income thresholds and construction new-employer UC rate not collected.
